A1.justification: Both complete 52-page PDFs describe the same scoping review. Their text, equations, tables, figures and references support reliable comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 4 report the authors' original descriptive analysis of 57 selected studies, including publication trends and frequencies of privacy attacks and preservation methods.

after.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 4 retain the authors' analysis of the 57-study corpus. These original data-analysis results qualify even though the reviewed attack-performance findings are attributed to other studies.

M1.justification: No algorithm, architecture, training objective or inference procedure is added or revised. The review framework, surveyed methods and proposed privacy-preserving XAI characteristics remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same 57-study corpus covering January 2019 through December 2024, with identical XAI and privacy categories. No dataset, evaluated task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an original benchmark comparison against baselines. The methods catalogued in Tables 2 and 3 have identical membership after matching rows shifted across page breaks.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same search, screening, eligibility, extraction and researcher-verification procedures. No evaluation metric, sample size or testing protocol changes.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test or error analysis is added or revised. The three illustrative loan-application use cases in Section 6 and Table 4 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The review retains the same descriptive frequency reporting. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimation for its own analysis.

E6.justification: Both report 57 retained studies from 1,943 screened records. Figure 4's distributions and trends, the table entries and the findings summarized in Sections 4–5 are unchanged; relocated entries are retained.

T1.justification: The threat model and mathematical formulations of membership inference, model inversion, model extraction and property inference in Equations 1–8 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.3 and conclusion retain the same research questions and contributions: categorizing privacy risks, reviewing preservation methods and proposing characteristics of privacy-preserving XAI.

C2.justification: Interpretations of privacy, explainability and utility trade-offs, method limitations, design recommendations and open issues in Sections 4–7 are unchanged. The broader impact statement is also retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same search string, databases, search date and Covidence workflow. Existing software-access information, including the DALEX footnote, is unchanged; no implementation or code/data availability details are added.

R1.justification: The cited works, complete reference list and comparisons with earlier reviews in Section 2.4 are unchanged. The added publication information does not revise the paper's positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 changes the two University of Guelph affiliation labels from Department to School of Computer Science and adds TMLR publication information and an OpenReview review-record line. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Publication headers and front-matter additions cause modest reflow. Figure 3 moves from page 10 to page 11, Table 1 gains continuation headers, and other table breaks shift. Figure artwork, captions and substantive table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds publication and review metadata and makes modest formatting adjustments while retaining the same evidence, analyses, reasoning, claims and limitations. These editorial changes do not materially improve or weaken the paper's scientific support, reproducibility or overall readability.
